This RFI seeks available oceanographic designs from the U.S. and allied nation maritime industrial bases, including an understanding of the level of maturity of each design. This RFI also requests information regarding industry capability to produce hydrographic and bathymetric-capable vessels from within the U.S. maritime industrial base. The ships will be designed and built to commercial regulatory body requirements (e.g. American Bureau of Shipping Marine Vessel Rules), obtain a U.S. Coast Guard Certificate of Inspection, and comply with other regulatory body regulations, such as International Marine Pollution Regulations and Safety of Life at Sea, as appropriate. T-AGS(X) will have a civilian mariner crew and embarked NAVOCEANO surveyors. Parameter | Requirement Mission Requirements | Ability to launch, operate, and recover mission equipment while holding position, with a sustained wind speed of 27 knots and a current speed at best heading in NATO Sea State (SS) 5. Operating Environment | Classed for unrestricted service. Engineered to operate navigable oceans including subarctic waters beginning 50°N. Hydrographic surveys conducted in depths less than 200 meters. Speed | Minimum 15 knots in all headings in seas, up to the top of NATO SS4. 10 knots on best heading, up to the top of NATO SS5. Dynamic Positioning | ABS DP-2 certification or equivalent. Maintain position and any heading within 33-ft radius with minimum current of 2 knots, 27-knot sustained wind, and seas up to NATO SS5. Maintain trackline within plus or minus 10 ft at 0.5 to 12 knots with a minimum 5,000 lb towing force. Endurance | Capable of 12,000 nautical miles at 12 knots plus 29 days at 3 knots, with a 10% fuel reserve. Draft | Less than 30 feet at full load. Acoustic Characteristics | Reduction of hull-induced flow noise and bubble sweep down. All installed sonars operate at full performance at up to 12 knots in NATO SS4. PROGRAM BACKGROUND The program seeks to recapitalize the existing oceanographic survey ship fleet. This fleet provides marine and hydrographic data collection to support preparation of maps, charts, books, geodetic products, and numerical and oceanographic prediction The Department of the Navy’s (DON) current oceanographic survey ship capabilities are provided by six PATHFINDER (T-AGS 60) Class ships. The PATHFINDER Class is approaching the end of its expected service life and recapitalization is needed to maintain the Navy’s required capability. REQUESTED

High density storage spaces located aft with access to working areas by hatches using ship cranes. Overside Handling | Capable of statically handling, deploying, and recovering large mission packages over the side at loads up to 10,000 lbs, including a 50 ft core sampler. Mission Related Deck Equipment | A suite of cranes, winches, stern A-frame, and other deck gear required to permit loading and unloading the ship without assistance to support a variety of oceanographic operations at sea. The winch system will have a slack tensioning subsystem, and the tow winch system is located below decks to protect from the elements. Provision for the remote control of permanently installed mission-related winches from weather-protected enclosure(s) with maximum practicable visibility of the cable to the last overside block or sheave. Contract Considerations –What other contract considerations might the government contemplate as part of its acquisition strategy? Acquisition strategy – The Navy is considering alternative acquisition approaches and/or the use of a vessel construction manager or streamlined government quality assurance processes. Please share your perspective on the potential impacts associated with these approaches. Do you have suggestions for how PMS 325 could modify its acquisition approach to reduce costs, minimize risks, and/or expedite delivery schedule? Schedule – please provide a notional schedule to complete a production-ready design production duration for a fleet of up to eight vessels by hull (e.g., a Gantt chart). Cost Estimate – please provide a rough order of magnitude cost estimate for design (parent craft design modification, if proposed, or production-ready design). Please provide a separate rough order of magnitude cost estimate for production of up to eight vessels. Please include relevant assumptions (e.g., inflation, labor rates). Note: This ROM is non-binding and for planning purposes only. Discreet and Covert Operations – please provide design examples for completing discreet and covert operations for this vessel. Specifically, the Navy is investigating if a moonpool is required for these operations or if there is an alternative method. The Navy would also like to know how this method would impact the design features and cost. RESPONSES Interested parties should respond to this RFI no later than 5:00 PM, Eastern Standard Time (EST), on AUG 31, 2026. RFI responses shall be submitted electronically via email to: Mr. Joe Saponaro NAVSEA 02, at joseph.f.sapon

A water system which provides drinking water but does not meet the definition of a public water system as defined by the SDWA. Non-public water systems areclassified as one of the following: 1. A non-public water system serving less than 25 persons (ADP) and not meeting the definition of NPNT water system (for example, smaller recreation sites, seasonal guard stations, or work centers with short-term, seasonal employees). The convoy must proceed directly to the Pier with no stopping. unny areas with low dense vegetation near shallow water areas. Their diet consists of insects, fish, frogs, salamanders and toads. They are dormant between Oct 15- March 31. SMALL By direction SMALL.PETER.D.1048778 646 Digitally signed by SMALL.PETER.D.1048778646 Date: 2026.04.02 16:18:58 -04'00' NAVSEA OP 5 REVISION 9 ABSTRACT OF SIGNIFICANT CHANGES Enclosure (1) 1. NAVSEA OP 5 has been reclassified from a Distribution C (restricted) technical manual to Distribution A (publicly releasable). This change follows a comprehensive review to remove all controlled unclassified information (CUI), making the document suitable for wider distribution. 2. References to authorities and offices have been updated to reflect recent name changes, e.g., references to the Department of Defense the Department of Defense Explosives Safety Review Board have been changed to Departm

. Paragraph 2-5.2.8.1 has been added to define conditions for applying the combat exemption to power application non-launch operations performed pier-side. 9. Electrical requirements have been updated for harmonization with NFPA 70 (NEC), specifically article 220.3(A) and article 250.30. 10. Paragraph 5-5.1 has been updated to include guidance for the installation of a power system ground. 11. Paragraph 5-5.4.2 has been revised to include grounding requirements for controlling hazards from electrical currents flowing between ordnance components during power application non-launch operations. 12. Paragraph 5-5.4.4 has been revised to mandate appropriate marking of ordnance grounds. 13. Paragraph 5-9.1 has been revised to permit electrical testing and reprogramming operations outside a test cell, provided these operations are approved by the Weapon System Explosives Safety Review Board (WSESRB). 14. Paragraph 5-9.1.1 has been added to establish grounding criteria for weapon systems during power application non-launch operations. 15. Paragraph 5-9.2.1 has been added to establish criteria for the powered interrogation and programming (PIAP) ground system during power application non-launch operations. method based on facility needs. 19. Paragraph 7-7.4.1 has been updated to align personnel protection requirements with Defense Explosives Safety Regulation (DESR) 6055.09. 20. Paragraph 7-9.3.1 has been revised to address specialized testing, clarifying NOSSA approval requirements for concurrence with power application non-launch activities. 21. Paragraphs 7-11.1.2 and 7-11.1.2.1 have been amended to ensure airfield clearance criteria comply with current airfield standards and DESR 6055.09. 22. Paragraph 7-13.6.c has been revised for consistency with DESR 6055.09 inert storage criteria. 23. Paragraph 7-13.10 has been revised from a mandatory to an advisory regulation, allowing an installation’s commanding officer to accept risk. 24. Paragraph 7-13.11 has been revised to clarify criteria for overhead electrical power lines supporting existing facilities versus new facilities. 25. Paragraph 7-13.16.8 has been revised to provide clarifying guidance for utilities and services at explosive facilities. 26. Paragraph 7-14.7.3.2 revised underground storage criteria for consistency with the DESR 6055.09. 27. Table 7-31 (Criteria for Non-DoD Explosives Activities on DoW Installations) has been added outlining criteria for launch facilities (space orbital) and associated explos

-compliant solvent and remove the unsubstantiated 15% moisture content allowance for Research, Development, Test and Evaluation (RDT&E) operations. 36. Paragraph 13-2.2.1a(1) has been revised to address minimum separation distances for non- essential personnel during unrelated ammunition and explosives operations. 37. Paragraph 13-3.3.1.d has been revised to require a 30-minute wait period for shock tube initiated blasting caps, consistent with EODB 60A-1-1-31, General Information on EOD Disposal Procedures. 38. Environmental compliance requirements have been updated to align with current Environmental Protection Agency policies. 39. Appendix A has been updated with definitions for power application non-launch, proximity testing, electrical interrogation, and PIAP ground. 40. Procedures for requesting and maintaining deviations have been revised and moved from appendix C to paragraph 1. Appendix C has been removed in its entirety. 41. All cargo ammunition and explosives must always be offloaded prior to drydocking or entry into a shipyard or SRF, except in emergency situations. Specific details on berthing and handling any ammunition within a shipyard are provided in paragraph 2-16 of NAVSEA OP 4. 2-5.1.2.1. Hazard Class/Division (HC/D) 1.1F concussion grenades may be stored in ship’s secure, operational magazines, or zero-arc magazines on ships in shipyards, including commercial shipyards, when necessary to meet security requirements without requesting site approval or an event waiver. If the ship is placed in drydock, the grenades must be offloaded or restricted to storage in zero-arc magazines. The following conditions are mandatory to the storage and handling of this security material. a. The minimum amount of HC/D 1.1F material necessary to meet mission requirements will be stored onboard ships, with a 10 pound NEW limit. b. Hot work cannot be performed adjacent to (on the same level and sharing a bulkhead), or directly above or below a zero-arc magazine containing HC/D 1.1F material. Purpose. To establish a NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center (FLC) Yokosuka Contracting Officer’s weight handling equipment oversight plan per reference (a). 2. Cancellation. NAVSUPFLCYINST 4200.9H. 3. Applicability. These requirements apply to all solicitations and contracts for supplies, construction, ship repair, demolition, or other services for the incidental use of non-Navy owned cranes at Navy shore installations. 4. Scope. This instruction is applicable to NAVSUP FLC Yokosuka Contracting Department, Yokosuka Division. 5. Background. NAVSUP FLC Yokosuka Co

Japan Regional Maintenance Center (SRF-JRMC) Yokosuka will include the provisions of enclosure (1). All solicitations/contracts for explicit and incidental use of non-Navy owned cranes for COMFLEACT tenants will include the NAVSUP FLC Yokosuka standard contract text “Non- Navy Owned Cranes” set forth in enclosure (2). (2) Will include the translated copies of enclosures (3) and (4) in all contracts. b. The Contractor: (1) Shall notify the host activity and Public Works Department Yokosuka (PRY 33) prior to any crane entering the activity per reference (a). (2) Shall post on every crane entering COMFLEACT Yokosuka, a Certificate of Compliance, enclosure (4), signifying the crane and rigging gear conform to the Government of Japan standards and personnel operating these cranes are fully trained and qualified. The contractor shall also certify that all crane operators working on COMFLEACT Yokosuka have been trained not to ignore or avoid safety devices (such as anti-two blocking devices) during lift operations. (3) Shall ensure a critical lift plan detailing procedures pertaining to safe crane operations is in place prior to any crane performing a critical lift. REQUIREMENTS: 3.1 Notify the SUPERVISOR one day prior to bringing any Weight Handling Equipment (WHE), (cranes, multi-purpose machines, material handling equipment that may be used in a crane-like application, rigging gear, below the hook lifting devices, and etc.) to lift suspended loads on Naval facilities. If emergent conditions require performance of work outside the scope of the contract, notify the Contracting Officer immediately. 3.2 Complete a certificate of compliance (Attachment A), and validate that the requirements of 2.1 through 2.7 and Paragraph 11.1 of 2.8 have been met prior to bringing or using any contractor WHE to lift suspended loads on Naval facilities. 3.2.1 Maintain written documentation of the last weight test of the crane and all related WHE on site. 3.3 Ensure that WHE and personnel comply with the following requirements: 3.3.1 Personnel performing weight handling must have an understanding of all signs, notices, and operating instructions, and be familiar with the applicable hand signals prescribed by Article 71 of 2.4 for the type of crane in use. Government Roles and Responsibilities The following personnel shall oversee and coordinate surveillance activities: Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) – The ACO shall assure performance of all necessary actions for effective contracting, ensure compliance with the contract terms, and shall safeguard the interests of the United States in the contractual relationship. The ACO shall also assure the contractor receives impartial, fair, and equitable treatment under this contract. The ACO is ultimately responsible for the final determination of the adequacy of the contractor’s performance. Project Manager (PM) / Contracting Officer Representative (COR) – The PM/COR is responsible for technical administration of the contract and shall assure proper Government surveillance of the contractor’s performance. The PM/COR shall keep a quality assurance file. The PM/COR is not empowered to make any contractual commitments or to authorize any contractual changes on the Government’s behalf. Performance Standards The performance and acceptable quality level standards are listed in Enclosure (1). The Government shall use these standards to assess contractor performance. C-5.0 : DELAYS / DISRUPTIONS The Contractor shall coordinate the work effort with SRF-JRMC Project Manager on a daily basis to prevent changing situations from causing delays and disruptions. Disruption due to minor delays in obtaining access to spaces and operation of equipment are to be expected. A minor delay is defined as eight clock (8) hours or less in duration (and is not the cumulative effect of labor hour impact). Minor delays and/or disruptions are considered normal rather than unusual occurrences during the performance of tasks ordered under the resulting contract. the process of repair and do not become an integral part of the repaired vessel. (5) The contract fixed fully burdened ship repair labor rate shall be used for negotiating growth work during the entire availability regardless of how many labor hours and material dollars are procured and negotiated. (6) The growth reservation man-hours and material dollar requirements listed above are part of this contract under the original solicitation and award. The man-hour reservation shall include both prime contractor and subcontractor efforts. Väljaspool Euroopa Liidu riike ning Euroopa Liidus peale paketis ettenähtud andmemahu ära kasutamist peab kehtima hakkama teenusepakkuja standardne ärikliendi päeva- või nädalamahtudel põhinev rändluslahendus (päevalagi), mis hoiab ära kontrollimatu andmemahu tarbimise. Lisamahu tellimine pakettidele A ja B peab olema kättesaadav iseteeninduses ja rakenduma reaalajas. Pakettide hinnad esitatakse hanke maksumuse vormil. Andmesideteenus seadmetele Sideteenus seadmetele, mis ei kasuta asutuse kõnesideteenust (tahvelarvutid, sülearvutid, kaamerad, nutiülekäigud jne) ning masinatele/seadmetele (IoT/telemeetria, nt tõkkepuud, veearvestid, valvekaamerad jne) Teenusepakkuja peab tagama mobiilse andmeside toimimise 4G (LTE)- ja 5G-võrkudes kõigil teenusepakkuja poolt pakutavatel sagedustel. Kõik paketid peavad olema kasutatavad pakkuja 5G-võrgus ilma täiendava liitumis- või kuutasuta. Tellitavad andmesideteenused hõlmavad järgmisi alamteenuseid: mobiilse andmeside pakett seadmetele (ilma kõneteenuseta) M2M (Machine-to-Machine) / telemeetria pakett staatilise avaliku IPv4 aadressi lisateenus Kõik käesolevas peatükis kirjeldatud seadmete ja M2M SIM-kaardid peavad võimaldama SMS-sõnumite saatmist ja vastuvõtmist (vajalik seadmete konfigureerimiseks ja märguanneteks). Hankija lükkab tagasi pakkumuse, mille alusel sõlmitav hankeleping oleks RSanS § 7 lg 1 alusel tühine. Määrust kohaldatakse riigihangetele alates rahvusvahelisest piirmäärast. Tööprojekt tuleb esitada Tellijale kooskõlastamiseks hiljemalt 1 kuu jooksul lepingu allkirjastamisest ning kohustuslikult kooskõlastatud enne remonttööde algust. Projekteerija peab tööprojektis ette nägema meetmed vee korduvsissenemise vältimiseks suletud profiilide (CFRHS) sisemusse — drenaažiavade rajamine profiilide alumistesse nurkadesse, poltliidete tihendamine või muu tehniliselt põhjendatud lahendus. Meetmed peavad hõlmama ka kahjustamata sõlmi kahe puutatud tugisamba ulatuses. II etapp: Remont- ja tugevdamistööd kohapeal Metallkonstruktsioonide pinna ettevalmistus vastavalt ISO 8501-1:2007 normile, puhtusaste vastavalt projekteerija poolt valitud korrosioonikaitse süsteemi nõuetele. Remont-, tugevdamis- või asendustööde teostamine kooskõlastatud tööprojekti alusel. Remonditud piirkondade pinnatöötlus ning professionaalse tööstusliku korrosioonikaitse pealekandmine vastavalt ISO 12944 standardile, korrosioonikategooria C5-I, kestvuskategooria vähemalt „kõrge" (H, 15–25 aastat). Värvitoonid peavad vastama galerii algupärasele lahendusele: välispinnal sinine RAL 5008. Hankija lähtub pakkumuse maksumuse tabelis esitatud ühikhindade põhjal arvutatud maksumusest juhul, kui pakkuja on arvutusvea parandamisega nõustunud. Pakkuja teatab hankijale kahe tööpäeva jooksul vastava teate saamisest arvates, kas ta nõustub arvutusvea parandamisega. Kui pakkuja arvutusvea parandamisega ei nõustu, lükkab hankija pakkumuse tagasi. Hankija võib RHS § 162 lg 1 alusel asjade hankelepingu korral pakkumuse tagasi lükata, kui üle 50 protsendi pakkumuse kogumaksumusest moodustavad asjad, mille päritolu kolmandatest riikidest on kindlaks määratud vastavalt Euroopa Parlamendi ja nõukogu määrusele (EL) nr 952/2013, millega kehtestatakse liidu tolliseadustik (ELT L 269, 10.10.2013, lk 1–101). Hankija lükkab tagasi pakkumuse, mille alusel sõlmitav hankeleping oleks RSanS § 7 lg 1 alusel tühine. Pakkuja, kelle pakkumus on tagasi lükatud, ei osale edasises väikehankemenetluses. Kui väikehange on jagatud osadeks, kontrollib hankija igale osale esitatud pakkumuste vastavust HAD esitatud tingimustele eraldi. ip_data_security.text: a isikuandmete kaitse tagamisest. Isikuandmete vastutav töötleja on Eesti Energia kontserni kuuluv Eesti Vabariigis registreeritud ettevõtja kes on koostööpartneriga koostöölepingu sõlminud. 1.2.1. Enefit partnerite portaali isikuandmete töötlemise põhimõtted on täpsustatud punktis 7 ning võivad sisaldada erandeid põhimõtetes kehtestatud tingimustest. 1.3. Kirjeldatud põhimõtted on koostatud Euroopa Parlamendi ja nõukogu 27. aprilli määruse (EL) 2016/679 füüsiliste isikute kaitse kohta isikuandmete töötlemisel ja selliste andmete vaba liikumise ning direktiivi 96/95/46/EÜ kehtetuks tunnistamise kohta (isikuandmete kaitse üldmäärus, GDPR) artiklis 12 „Selge teave, teavitamine ja andmesubjekti õiguste teostamise kord“ sätestatud vastutava töötleja nõuete täitmiseks ja füüsiliste isikute teavitamiseks isikuandmete töötlemise põhimõtetest ja õiguste tagamisest. 1.4. „Eesti Energia kontserni koostööpartnerite isikuandmete töötlemise põhimõtted“ kehtivad Eesti Energia kontserni kuuluvate ettevõtjate, kes on loetletud punktis 1.2., koostööpartnerite ning koostööpartnerite töötajate ja teiste andmesubjektide suhtes, kelle isikuandmeid töödeldakse käesolevas dokumendis kirjeldatud eesmärkidel. 1.5. Eesti Energia kontsern lähtub isikuandmete töötlemisel järgnevatest põhi

simineku, muudatuste või hävitamise eest. 2. Mõisted 2.1. Käesolevates põhimõtetes kasutatakse mõisteid sellises tähenduses, nagu need on defineeritud isikuandmete kaitse üldmääruses. 2.2. Andmesubjekt - füüsiline isik, kelle isikuandmeid Eesti Energia kontsern töötleb. 2.3. Koostööpartner - välise teenuse osutaja (nt hoolduspartner), kellega Eesti Energia kontserni ettevõtjal on teenuse osutamiseks sõlmitud leping. Samuti käsitleb Eesti Energia kontsern koostööpartnerina koostööpartneri esindajat, koostööpartneri töötajaid ning teisi koostööpartneriga seotud isikuid. 2.4. Andmekaitse õigusaktid - isikuandmete kaitse seadus, GDPR jt siseriiklikul ja Euroopa Liidu tasandil valdkonnale kohalduvad õigusaktid. 2.5. Isikuandmed - igasugune teave tuvastatud või tuvastatava füüsilise isiku kohta. 2.6. Isikuandmete töötlemine - isikuandmetega läbiviidav toiming (nt andmete edastamine, salvestamine, sisestamine). 2.7. Vastutav töötleja - Eesti Energia kontserni kuuluv Eesti Vabariigis registreeritud ettevõtja, kes on koostööpartneriga koostöölepingu sõlminud. 2.8. Volitatud töötleja - V astutava töötleja lepingupartner (vastutava töötleja suhtes eraldiseisev üksus), kes töötleb isikuandmeid vastutava töötleja nimel. 3. Teave andmete ja nende kogumisviiside koh

tletud eesmärkide saavutamiseks töötleb Eesti Energia kontsern teatud andmeid kasutades tehisintellekti tööriistu ja/või tööriistu, mis sisaldavad tehisintellekti funktsionaalsust. 4. Isikuandmete töötlemise eesmärk ja õiguslik alus 4.1. Isikuandmete töötlemine, mille õiguslikuks aluseks on leping 4.1.1. Olukorras, kus Eesti Energia kontsern sõlmib koostööpartneriga lepingu või valmistab seda ette, täidab koostööpartneriga sõlmitud lepingut või haldab lepinguga seonduvat oma süsteemides, tugineb Eesti Energia kontsern isikuandmete töötlemisel lepingu täitmise või lepingu sõlmimisele eelnevate meetmete võtmise õiguslikule alusele (GDPR art 6(1)b). 4.1.2. Eesti Energia kontsern töötleb isikuandmeid lepingulisel alusel: 4.1.2.1. koostööpartneri ja/või tema esindaja isiku tuvastamiseks; 4.1.2.2. lepingueelselt pakkumuse koostamiseks ning teabe andmiseks; 4.1.2.3. koostööpartneriga sõlmitud lepingu täitmiseks; 4.1.2.4. lepinguga seotud tasude arvestamiseks, teadete ja arvete koostamiseks ja saatmiseks; 4.1.2.5. koostööpartneri töötajate tööajaandmete avaldamiseks koostööpartnerile; 4.1.2.6. lepingu täitmise tagamiseks (nt tagatiste seadmiseks, garantiikirjad); 4.1.2.7. vajadusel muude tegevuste tarbeks, mis on vajalikud lepingu ettevalmistamiseks, sõlmimiseks,

ise tagamiseks (nt tagatiste seadmiseks, garantiikirjad); 4.1.2.7. vajadusel muude tegevuste tarbeks, mis on vajalikud lepingu ettevalmistamiseks, sõlmimiseks, täitmiseks, haldamiseks või lõpetamiseks. 4.1.3. Punktides 4.1.2.2. ja 4.1.2.4. nimetatud eesmärkide saavutamiseks võib Eesti Energia kontsern kasutada tehisintellekti tööriistu ja/või tööriistu, mis sisaldavad tehisintellekti funktsionaalsust. 4.2. The Postbox is an online submission facility which allows buyers to receive responses from suppliers electronically in a secure environment. Responses are submitted through the portal and held in the secure Postbox until the deadline for responses has expired. Nominated members of the buyer organisation then unlock the Postbox to access the submissions. The Postbox can be used for the receipt of PQQs, tender responses, Quick Quote submissions and all supporting documents. A full audit trail is kept of all access to the Postbox and a complete record of all supplier submissions is stored. Please note: Before you can use the postbox you must record your interest in a notice. In the case of a Quick Quote or the second stage of a dual stage procedure you must have been invited by the buyer to submit a response. Postbox Response Workspace All postbox re
